docs.title: Admin Maintenance API
docs.description: Use the Admin Maintenance API for customer retention operations. These endpoints perform hard deletes and require ACCESSBPMADMIN.

docs.title: Admin Security API
docs.description: Use the Admin Security API to manage users, groups, passwords, group membership, and permission assignments.

docs.title: Agent Processes API
docs.description: Use the Agent Processes API to deploy reusable Agent Process definitions and retrieve the latest or versioned definitions by key.

docs.title: AI Credentials API
docs.description: Use the AI Credentials API to store provider credentials server-side and reference masked credential IDs from AI tasks.

docs.title: Authentication API
docs.description: Use the Authentication API to sign users in and inspect the current JWT session.

docs.title: Code Tasks API
docs.description: Use the Code Tasks API to upload JVM JARs, discover classes and methods, and inspect execution audit history.

docs.title: Documents API
docs.description: Use the Documents API to upload files, read metadata, preview, download, list, and delete task documents.

docs.title: Forms API
docs.description: Use the Forms API to deploy and retrieve versioned form definitions by stable form ID.

docs.title: Incidents API
docs.description: Use the Incidents API to review, acknowledge, retry, resolve, and reopen operational incidents.

docs.description: Use the Processes API to deploy definitions, start instances, manage variables, operate runtime state, and correlate messages.

docs.description: Use the Tasks API to list visible work, claim shared tasks, inspect task context, and complete user tasks.

docs.title: Capacity Planning
docs.description: Easy BPM scales horizontally for API traffic and asynchronous worker execution. Backend replicas can be increased for REST traffic and message consumption. Worker replicas can be increased for external API and service task throughput.

docs.title: Docker Deployment
docs.description: Docker Compose is the fastest way to run a complete Easy BPM stack for demos, pilots, and small beta environments.

docs.title: Kubernetes Deployment
docs.description: Easy BPM includes a Helm chart at deploy/helm/easybpm for Kubernetes deployments.

docs.title: Observability
docs.description: Easy BPM exposes Spring Boot Actuator endpoints and Prometheus metrics from the backend runtime.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.description: Easy BPM is configured with environment variables that follow the EASYBPM standard. Third-party container variables, such as POSTGRESDB, keep the names required by those images.

docs.title: First Login
docs.description: Easy BPM creates a first administrator user on startup. Use this account to sign in, create real customer users, and assign permissions.

docs.title: Installation
docs.description: Easy BPM can run as individual local processes during development or as containers for shared environments.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.description: This guide starts Easy BPM locally with PostgreSQL, RabbitMQ, the backend, the worker, and the web applications.

docs.title: API Tasks
docs.description: API Tasks call external HTTP services through the Easy BPM worker. They are useful for CRM calls, ERP updates, payment checks, webhook-style integrations, and private service orchestration.

docs.title: Call Activities
docs.description: Call Activities start another Easy BPM process as a subprocess. Use them when you want reusable process fragments such as KYC review, document verification, onboarding, or exception handling.

docs.title: Code Tasks
docs.description: Code Tasks execute Java or Kotlin code packaged in a JVM JAR. They are useful when a workflow needs customer-specific calculations, normalization, validation, enrichment, or deterministic business logic that should run inside the platform boundary.

docs.title: Create a Process
docs.description: An Easy BPM process is deployed as an Easy BPM process JSON graph. You can create it visually in the Modeler or send JSON directly to the /processes API.

docs.title: Documents
docs.description: Easy BPM stores documents uploaded through task forms or API calls. Metadata is returned through JSON endpoints, while file content is retrieved through download or preview endpoints.

docs.title: Forms
docs.description: Forms define the fields shown to users in the Task Portal. They are versioned by a stable formId, so a process can reference the latest deployed version without changing the process definition.

docs.title: Message Events
docs.description: Message events let external systems resume a waiting process by message name and correlation key.

docs.title: User Tasks
docs.description: User tasks create human work items that appear in the Task Portal.

docs.title: Welcome
docs.description: Easy BPM is a developer-friendly business process platform for modeling, running, and operating business workflows. It includes a process modeler, runtime API, task portal, admin console, asynchronous worker, document handling, code-task execution, and security administration.

docs.title: Admin Console
docs.description: The Admin Console is the operational workspace for process monitoring, instance intervention, incident recovery, maintenance cleanup, user and group management, and Code Task audits.

docs.title: Modeler
docs.description: The Easy BPM Modeler is the workspace for designing process definitions and reusable forms. It has a component palette, a canvas, a properties panel, validation feedback, import/export actions, and deployment to the configured Easy BPM backend.

docs.title: Operations
docs.description: Easy BPM includes operational tools for investigating process execution, recovering failed work, and cleaning old runtime data.

docs.title: Task Portal
docs.description: The Task Portal is where business users and developer testers start processes, view assigned work, claim group tasks, complete forms, upload documents, and preview PDFs.

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.description: Use the EASYBPM naming standard for customer-facing configuration. Third-party container variables, such as POSTGRESDB, still use the names required by those images.

docs.title: Examples
docs.description: The public docs include copy-paste examples for the most common customer workflows.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.description: Easy BPM uses permission codes assigned directly to users or through groups.

docs.title: Process JSON Reference
docs.description: Easy BPM process definitions are JSON objects with processId, nodes, and flows.

docs.description: Use the Admin Security API to manage users, groups, passwords, group membership, and permission assignments.
